analysis: The supplied PR units contain only documentation and a changelog entry: changelog.d/large-memory-checkpoint-stage-cap.md and docs/reference/configuration.md (the patch at hunk @@ -505). No source code was supplied, so the actual SSDPrefixCachePolicy.swift change was not reviewed. The docs say complete-checkpoint SSD restores on Macs with at least 96 GiB now default to a 3 GiB / 2,500 ms staging cap (previously 1 GiB / 1,000 ms). Explicit DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_MAX_STAGE_MB / _MS values still win, attention block caches keep defaults, and the daily write cap is unchanged. Relevant threat: T-041 (prefix cache, TB-007, A-001). This change affects only transient staging RAM and read-time bounds, and nothing in the docs shows a change to the at-rest crypto, HMAC lookup tags, 30-minute TTL, account salt scoping or disk budget. The docs state that native destination plus scratch is separately reserved before allocation, with no permanent RAM carve, so the memory-reservation mitigation appears to be preserved. Possible effect on the SEC-035 TTFT oracle: deeper restores (up to 16,384 tokens) make hit/miss latency differences larger, but this is the already-accepted same-account channel. The threat model's T-041 detection_hint does not list staging caps as a sign-off trigger. The next pass should verify the code: (1) that the large-memory detection cannot be spoofed or misread and that admission still goes through GlobalKVCacheBudget; (2) that the 3 GiB staging reservation fails closed under memory pressure; (3) that explicit env values keep precedence. Because the code was not supplied, this is a coverage limit rather than evidence of safety.
